label: BW-style / CLI-adapted

rubric_scores.evidence: The classroom is recognizable through its divided green chalkboard, blue lower wall, overhead notice, and wooden teaching furniture.
The notice sits above the board, with the central desk and chair below and additional desks in the foreground and at right. These principal relationships remain recognizable.
Complementary views reveal extremely low desks and foreground chairs reduced above the floor to small backrest fragments, incompatible with functional classroom furniture proportions.
Green board, blue wall band, pale plaster, tan wood, and thin gray furniture supports preserve the main color and surface distinctions, although substantially simplified.
Bright, soft illumination keeps the major content legible with coherent shadows. It is flatter and less warm than the target but does not obscure the scene.
Oblique views demonstrate actual tabletop thickness, legs, chair backs, and depth separation from the board wall.
Actual wall, board, desk, and chair meshes have finite nonempty geometry, assigned materials, and addressable parent chains. Material records contain connected shader nodes.

dimension_scores.evidence: The main composition is close and readily identifiable, but distorted furniture and generic board texture weaken the reconstruction.
Foreground chair seats lie below the floor, and chair backs emerge as fragments. Desk supports also extend substantially below floor level; the oblique renders corroborate the placement problem.
The characteristic green, blue, cream, and wood palette survives, but colors are washed out and furniture silhouettes are overly rectangular.
Simple geometry, repetitive cloudy board markings, visible render noise, and sunken furniture reduce credibility.
Principal horizontal placement and depth ordering match well; furniture elevations relative to the floor are substantially wrong.
Board and notice proportions are convincing, but desk heights and exposed chair proportions are implausible in the complementary views.
Lighting is readable and consistent, but weak tonal contrast, uniform furniture surfaces, and generic board mottling lose the aged material character.
The major wall features and three desk positions are present. Foreground chairs are largely concealed by incorrect floor placement, and wear details are simplified.

same_model_bias_limit: Research and independent judge use Astra; separate sessions do not establish human independence.
